premises.text: Open-source software has bugs and missing features while support is hard to get because of a mismatch in knowledge and priority between users and developers
premises.evidence_span: all this software has two properties in common, which is bugs and missing features

premises.text: Users can place paid incentives on issue pages via integrations with major issue trackers, including multi-user crowdfunding on one issue
premises.evidence_span: a service which allows you to pay or get paid directly from an issue page

premises.text: Developers can one-click ask for an incentive or list an issue for crowdfunding from the same panel
premises.evidence_span: with one click, they can reach out and ask for an incentive or list the issue for crowdfunding

premises.text: The company takes a 6% fee on successful incentives and shares fees with issue-system hosters running the integration
premises.evidence_span: we take a 6% fee for each successful incentive

premises.text: Distribution aims to put the panel on every bug and feature page, later expanding beyond open source to app stores
premises.evidence_span: have our panel on every book page, every feature request, and in every support system

value.text: Users get needed software support or improvements and developers get paid to fix issues
value.evidence_span: place incentives for on demand software support

causal_links.evidence_span: what we have is a mismatch in knowledge and priority between the user and the developer
with two clicks, a user can place an incentive
adding a monetization element to the entire open source market

notes: Open-source examples list folded as framing of ubiquity, not separate premises. Bugs/missing features/support mismatch folded as one problem (§4.1.6). User place-incentive and developer ask-incentive are two sides of one marketplace mechanism but separately asserted jobs—kept as two premises under one product domain. ASR 'book' for bug left in spans. Anti-template: problem, marketplace product, and fee/distribution separately revisable.
